+def get_stats(ids, counts=None):
+    """
+    Given a list of integers, return a dictionary of counts of consecutive pairs
+    Example: [1, 2, 3, 1, 2] -> {(1, 2): 2, (2, 3): 1, (3, 1): 1}
+    Optionally allows to update an existing dictionary of counts
+    """
+    counts = {} if counts is None else counts
+    _count_elements(counts, zip(ids, ids[1:])) # counts[pair] += 1, in C
+    return counts
+
+
+def merge(ids, pair, idx):
+    """
+    In the list of integers (ids), replace all consecutive occurrences
+    of pair with the new integer token idx
+    Example: ids=[1, 2, 3, 1, 2], pair=(1, 2), idx=4 -> [4, 3, 4]
+    """
+    p0, p1 = pair
+    # jump between occurrences of p0 (k = occurrences left at >= i)
+    k = ids.count(p0)
+    if not k:
+        return list(ids)
+    newids = []
+    extend = newids.extend
+    append = newids.append
+    index = ids.index
+    last = len(ids) - 1
+    same = p0 == p1
+    i = 0
+    while k:
+        j = index(p0, i)
+        k -= 1
+        if j < last and ids[j+1] == p1:
+            extend(ids[i:j])
+            append(idx)
+            i = j + 2
+            if same:
+                k -= 1 # ids[j+1] was an occurrence of p0 too
+        else:
+            extend(ids[i:j+1])
+            i = j + 1
+    extend(ids[i:])
+    return newids
+
+
+def pop_top_pairs(heap, stats_get, heappush, heappop):
+    """
+    Lazy max-heap over pair counts: heap holds (-count, pair) entries, some
+    entry per pair with a count >= its current count. Returns (top, cands):
+    max(stats.values()) and every pair with that count; the candidates'
+    entries are pushed back, so the invariant still holds afterwards.
+    """
+    while True:
+        if not heap:
+            raise ValueError("max() arg is an empty sequence")
+        neg, p = heap[0]
+        c = stats_get(p)
+        if c == -neg:
+            break
+        heappop(heap)
+        if c and c < -neg:
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p)) # count went down: re-file it (not 0)
+    top = -neg
+    cands = []
+    while heap and heap[0][0] == neg:
+        p = heappop(heap)[1]
+        c = stats_get(p)
+        if c == top:
+            if p not in cands:
+                cands.append(p)
+        elif c and c < top:
+            heappush(heap, (-c, p))
+    for p in cands:
+        heappush(heap, (neg, p))
+    return top, cands
+

journal.text:
I went after encode_ir in minbpe. I read regex.py, base.py, _train.py, _heap.py, _slow.py and basic.py, then spread edits across all of them. Mostly that meant trimming imports and helpers, rewriting base.py from 177 lines down to 80, and reshuffling code in _train.py and _heap.py.

Evaluation 1 came back with identical outputs. encode_ir went from 378448980 to 374769173, a ratio of 0.9903. That missed the required 0.9900 and was rejected as no_improvement. train_ir ratio was 1.0005. Evaluation 3, after more edits, was worse: encode_ir ratio 1.0004 and train_ir ratio 1.0002, also rejected. I stopped without submitting.

What I believe now is that import and module cleanup barely moves instruction counts here. The 0.9903 gain was close to noise, and my later edits threw it away. Encode cost has to live in the actual merge loop, not in the file structure.

Next time I would profile encode in regex.py and _heap.py and target the per-chunk merge application directly. I would also keep the evaluation 1 diff as a starting point instead of over-editing past it.
